description: ODC (shared contracts pilot, phase 2): REFACTOR an inherited structure and its attributes - reorder, duplicate, repoint whoever uses it as a type, delete. The base is job:structure-lifecycle, so the WfCovLocation (formerly WfCovAddress) already has 5 attributes (Street, Postcode, District, Geo, WfCountry), is used as the type of the input Address of the public server action WfCovQuote_Build and of the nested attribute WfCovPolicyQuote.Address, and the attribute District is read by the expression 'Holder + " - " + Quote.Address.District'. It measures four things: (A) `move` of a structure attribute changes the position in the Attributes sequence (IndexInParent) - and the order of the JSON/REST contract - without touching keys or consumers; (B) `duplicate` of a structure copies the attributes (name with the platform suffix), inherits Public/Shareable and the Description, and is born without author consumers; (C) `replace` of one structure by another repoints the TYPED consumers (action input, nested attribute) to the new type, requiring the new type to be shareable when the action is public; (D) `delete` of an attribute without consumers is accepted, and so is the delete of the original structure after it is repointed, without force, because the replace repoints even the IAttribute of the anonymous record that the platform generates for each structure (measured: usages 10 -> 0 at the origin, 0 -> 11 at the destination) - the refusal with consumers is in tests/jobs-odc-negative/delete-structure-attribute-in-use.json and delete-structure-in-use.json.

ops._why: (0) ANTES, a ordem herdada: Street, Postcode, District, Geo, WfCountry (IndexInParent 0..4).
(1a) BEFORE: IndexInParent 4, the last one. Keep the key: the get (1c) must repeat it.
(1b) CHANGE 1 - REORDER: the attribute moves to the start of the Attributes sequence. Only the position changes; the key, the type and the consumers stay.
(1c) AFTER: IndexInParent 0, the same key as get (1a).
(1d) the relative form: Postcode now follows Geo. The sibling has to be a child of the same parent.
(1e) AFTER, the order: WfCountry, Street, District, Geo, Postcode. The same 5 keys as dump (0).
(1f) the parameter consumer does not know the order changed: same DataType key as what the base left.

(2a) CHANGE 2 - DUPLICATE the structure: the copy has the 5 attributes in the new order, all-new keys, inherits Public/Shareable True and the Description of the original (measured: the duplicate copies the sharing and the text), and is born without author consumers.

(2b) the copy: Name with the platform suffix (WfCovLocation2), Attributes 5, Public True and Shareable True inherited, Description equal to the original's - the same thing O11 does (tests/jobs/structure-refactor.json).
(2c) the 5 copied attributes, in the order of dump (1e).
(2d) real 0 (apart from the IAttribute of the anonymous record '<Copy> Record' generated by the platform): nobody cites the copy.

ops.name: WfCovSite
ops._why: (2e) give the copy an author name; the platform suffix is not a name. rename works because IStructure publishes a writable Name.

(2f) PRECONDITION of the replace (3), written on purpose even if the copy already inherited it: the action WfCovQuote_Build is public (shareable) and in ODC a shareable action only exposes shareable types. Without this, Verify would refuse the module after the repointing; here it is idempotent (get 2b already showed Public True).

(3a) BEFORE the replace: the inherited consumers - the input Address, the nested attribute WfCovPolicyQuote.Address, the IAttribute of the anonymous record, and the expressions that read the fields by path.

(3b) CHANGE 3 - REPOINT: the direct external consumers of the WfCovLocation now point to the WfCovSite. Same interface (IStructure), without force. The kernel checks in the model that 0 consumers remained at the origin and that all arrived at the destination. What the replace does NOT do: map the children - the expressions that cite Quote.Address.District still cite the parameter and the attribute by name, and the attribute District of the copy has that same name, so Verify stays clean.
(3c) AFTER: the DataType of the input now points to the key of the WfCovSite (the one from get 2b), not to the WfCovLocation.
(3d) AFTER: the nested attribute also changed type to the WfCovSite - a consumer inside the data model counts like any other.

(3e) count 0, real 0: NOBODY cites the WfCovLocation - the replace also repointed the IAttribute of the anonymous record generated by the platform, not just the author consumers. Compare with the usages (3a): count 10.
(3f) count 11, real 11: the 10 consumers of the usages (3a) plus the IAttribute of the anonymous record of the copy itself, all with the same keys.
(3g) the expressions did NOT change text: 'Holder + " - " + Quote.Address.District' stays the same - they never cited the name of the type.

(4a) CHANGE 4 - DELETE an attribute WITHOUT consumers (no expression reads Street): accepted without force. The refusal of the delete of an attribute WITH a consumer (District, read by an expression) is measured in the negative job.
(4b) AFTER: 4 attributes (WfCountry, District, Geo, Postcode); the keys of the ones that remained are those of dump (2c).

(4c) DELETE the original structure after it is repointed, WITHOUT force: the usages (3e) gave 0, because the replace took even the IAttribute of the anonymous record with it. Unlike an entity (delete-entity-whole.json, static-record-refactor.json), a repointed structure is deleted cleanly. brokenConsumers 0. The refusal of the delete of a structure with consumers is in tests/jobs-odc-negative/delete-structure-in-use.json.

ops.name: WfCovLocation
ops._why: (4d) empty list: the structure and its anonymous record disappeared.
(5) END: the public action still exposes 3 inputs and 1 output, now typed by the WfCovSite (public).
